text:
Sea's e-commerce (Shopee) service revenue grew 33.9%, from US$10.9 billion in 2024 to US$14.5 billion in 2025, driven primarily by GMV growth and secondarily by improved monetization [Sea, FY2025, p.99, 100].

Specifically:
- **GMV growth of 26.8%** — from US$100.5 billion in 2024 to US$127.4 billion in 2025 — was the main driver. This GMV expansion reflected overall online consumption growth across Sea's markets, as well as continual improvements in Shopee's service offerings such as faster delivery, enhanced user engagement through better e-commerce content, and greater efficiency in advertising and search [Sea, FY2025, p.99, 100].
- **Higher monetization rate** — e-commerce service revenue as a percentage of GMV improved from 10.8% in 2024 to 11.4% in 2025, reflecting increased monetization through paid advertising, transaction-based fees, and value-added services such as logistics and fulfillment [Sea, FY2025, p.99, 100; p.95, 96].
- **Order volume growth of 27.2%** — from 10.9 billion orders in 2024 to 13.9 billion in 2025 — while average order value remained roughly stable at about US$9, indicating the revenue growth came from transaction volume rather than higher spend per order [Sea, FY2025, p.99, 100].
- In terms of underlying profitability, higher e-commerce gross profit in 2025 was also attributed to GMV growth combined with the increased monetization rate, though this was partly offset by higher sales and marketing expenses from increased promotional activity and third-party advertising spend [Sea, FY2025, p.107].
